newsitem.title: USA: Quaker sees $1.4 bln Q1 charge on Snapple.
newsitem.headline: Quaker sees $1.4 bln Q1 charge on Snapple.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said it will take a non-cash pretax charge of about $1.4 billion, or $8.40 per share, to record its loss on the sale of the Snapple beverage business to Triarc Cos Inc for $300 million.
The food company paid $1.8 billion, including acquisition costs, for the premium beverage line two-and-a-half years ago.

"We decided it was in the shareholders' interest to remove the financial burdens and risks Snapple brought to the portfolio and better focus on our value-driving businesses," said Quaker chief executive William Smithburg.
The timing of the sale will enable Quaker to recoup taxes paid on previous capital gains of about $250 million, making the cash value of the transaction about $550 million, it said.
As a result of the sale, earnings before the one-time loss are expected to increase by about an additional $0.10 per share in 1997 as debt is reduced and Snapple losses removed, the company said.
"Quaker's future earnings per share will also benefit from these actions," it said.
Cash flow, already projected to be positive, will grow by the sale proceeds in the second quarter and by the expected recapture of capital gain taxes in early 1998, Quaker said.

"With annual sales of approximately $550 million, Snapple continues to be a leading alternative beverage brand with the ability to generate growth, but that opportunity is best pursued by a company with synergies in the independent distribution network," Smithburg said.
The transaction with Triarc is expected to close as soon as possible after regulatory approvals, Quaker said.
